Making Japanese curry? 🍛  Don’t just chop everything into random sizes. The way you cut your vegetables actually matters, especially if you want them nicely cooked and not disappear in curry. 🥕 𝐂𝐚𝐫𝐫𝐨𝐭 → rangiri cut Cutting it into irregular rolling pieces gives you different surfaces while keeping the pieces relatively similar in size, so they cook evenly. 🥔 𝐏𝐨𝐭𝐚𝐭𝐨 → bite-size chunks Not too small, so they have enough structure to hold their shape while becoming tender. 🧅 𝐎𝐧𝐢𝐨𝐧 → wedges Keeping the onion in wedges allows it to soften and become sweet without completely disappearing into the curry. It’s a small step, but proper cutting makes a difference in cooking time, texture and how your curry comes together. 📍Riga, Latvia 🇱🇻 If you’re looking for a European Christmas market that’s a little less obvious, put Riga on your list. 🎄✨ The Christmas market is right in the heart of Riga’s Old Town, around Dome Square, with wooden stalls selling artisan crafts, gifts and plenty of festive treats. You can try traditional Latvian food like 🫛🥓 grey peas with bacon, 🥟 piragi and 🍪 gingerbread, along with steaming cups of mulled wine and Riga Black Balsam. 🎶 There are also live performances, traditional Latvian folk music, carol singing and dancing throughout the festive season. Riga is definitely one to consider for a festive European getaway! ✨ 🧷 Save this reel & share it with someone who loves Christmas markets 🎄 #riga #rīgā #rigaoldtown #rigachristmasmarket #christmasmarkets
